From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal runbook, proration, and capacity timing for Stellaris private offer

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, Stellaris is planning to commit to the expanded capacity (2x concurrency / 3x monthly tokens) under the AWS Private Offer starting in July. To keep everything on one clean path, we put together a short runbook and a proposed proration approach so invoicing and acceptance align with your finance/quarter planning. Attached: renewal_workback.xlsx, amendment_template.pdf, acceptance_evidence_checklist.pdf.

High level ask:
- Confirm target effective date: 2026-07-01 (we can shift to 07-15 if you need mid-month proration).
- Confirm legal/procurement contact and internal PO number so we can push the private-offer amendment through DocuSign.
- Confirm you want the capacity uplift applied immediately on the effective date (we recommend a 14-day staged acceptance window to validate peak traffic).

Proration note (short):
- If effective 2026-07-01, July will be charged for the full month at the new rate. If you prefer mid-month activation we will prorate based on days-of-service; see billing_proration_calculation.csv (attached).

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm PO and effective date (reply to thread).
2) Redwood issues amendment via DocuSign (we'll pre-fill PO and new SKU quantities).
3) Once signed, we schedule a short ops handoff with our onboarding SRE to open KV cache warming windows and set burst capacity.

If it helps, Marissa can include details on the billing cutover playbook and suggested invoice schedule.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: renewal_workback.xlsx (spreadsheet), amendment_template.pdf (PDF), acceptance_evidence_checklist.pdf (PDF)

- Does the AWS Private Offer mechanism require us to annualize to keep marketplace billing (we want to avoid forced annualization if possible)?

Our procurement contact is procurement@stellaris.ai and our internal PO number is STL-PO-0526-9 (attached). We will need SOC 2 evidence and the latest security questionnaire answers before legal signs (we have those requests in parallel).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — can you send the DocuSign once you populate the amendment so our legal can prelim-review?

Hi Danielle —

Great — we're aligned on 2026-07-01 as a target effective date. Quick answers to your procurement questions and the runbook details:

Proration:
- We do daily proration for mid-month activations (charges reflect the exact days of service). Example: sign on July 15 -> charge = (17/31) * monthly committed fee; see attached billing_proration_calculation.csv for worked examples.
- If you sign on or before July 1, July will be billed at the new committed rate.

AWS Private Offer behavior:
- The Marketplace private offer itself doesn't force a multi-year annualization; you can accept an amendment to your existing private offer with the term you negotiate. For bookkeeping, many customers prefer aligning the term to their fiscal year — we can preserve your renewal cadence and apply the uplift for the remainder of the current term if you'd like.

Runbook summary (high level timeline):
- 2026-06-03: Redwood sends pre-populated amendment via DocuSign (we will include PO STL-PO-0526-9).
- 2026-06-04 to 06-10: Stellaris legal review + countersign window.
- 2026-06-11 to 06-18: Ops handoff / KV warming / test traffic (staged acceptance).
- 2026-07-01: Effective date — capacity uplift applied.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/stellaris/amendment/ABC123 (placeholder link)

Attachments: billing_proration_calculation.csv, amendment_template.pdf (redlined fields highlighted in the docx margin).

Legal contact for countersign: please loop in Jordan Ellis (jordan.ellis@stellaris.ai) so we can coordinate any minor redlines promptly.

Ben — can you confirm a tentative ops kickoff window (we propose 60–90 minutes) and whether we need to provision burst capacity on day 1?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Commercial Contracts Lead
Redwood Inference
